figures.caption: Percentage of missing responses per variable (red = more than 30 % missing).
Distribution of annual compensation: heavily right-skewed in USD (a), far less skewed after a log transform (b), with extreme tails visible in (c).
Rows retained at each step of salary-cohort construction.
Univariate profile of the 20,794 professional developers in the salary cohort.
Raw (unadjusted) median compensation by work arrangement, organisation size and education. Country mix confounds these gaps (see O3).
Spearman rank-correlation matrix of numeric and ordinal variables including log-compensation.
Bias-corrected Cramér's V between categorical variables (0 = independent, 1 = perfectly associated).
Q–Q plot of log-salary (a) and country-wise densities (b): log-salary is left-skewed and heavy-tailed rather than normal, with unequal location and spread across countries.
Distribution of annual compensation (USD, log axis) by country, ordered by median. India is highlighted in orange.
Median annual compensation with 95 % bootstrap confidence intervals; labels give the ratio to the USA median.
Relationship between professional experience and pay: hexbin density with LOWESS trend (a) and median pay by experience band for selected countries with 95 % bootstrap CIs (b).
Quadratic log-linear model: cumulative premium with 95 % CI (a) and marginal percentage return per additional year, pooled and by country (b).
Adjusted pay difference by job role relative to full-stack developers (country and experience held constant; 95 % HC3 CIs; grey = not significant at 5 %).
Adjusted pay differences by work arrangement (a), organisation size (b) and education (c).
Cumulative R² and incremental ΔR² as predictor blocks are added to the OLS model for log-compensation.
AI-tool adoption in the development process by age (a), experience (b), organisation size (c) and Stack Overflow visit frequency (d); labels show % currently using AI.
AI adoption rate with 95 % Wilson CIs by country (a) and job role (b); dashed line = overall adoption; India in orange.
Strength of association (Cramér's V) between AI adoption and each descriptive factor.
AI adoption by job role and age bracket (blank = fewer than 30 respondents).
Distribution of attitudes towards AI among respondents who use or plan to use AI tools.
Trust in AI accuracy (a) and sentiment (b) across experience bands (100 % stacked; red = negative, blue = positive).
Share of respondents who see AI as a threat to their own job, by job role (a) and age (b); dashed line = overall.
Spearman correlation matrix of AI attitude scores with experience and age.
Regression model comparison: cross-validated RMSE with ±1 SD (a), hold-out R² (b) and hold-out MAE in USD (c). Grey = baselines, orange = selected model.
Diagnostics of the selected regression model on the hold-out set: predicted vs actual pay (a), residual distribution (b) and residuals vs fitted values with LOWESS (c).
Learning curve of the tuned gradient-boosting model: the validation error is still slowly falling, so more data would help slightly.
Classification model comparison: cross-validated ROC-AUC (a), hold-out F1 (b) and hold-out ROC-AUC (c). Grey = baseline, orange = selected model.
ROC curves with AUC in the legend (a) and precision–recall curves (b) for all classifiers on the hold-out set.
Selected classifier on the hold-out set: normalised confusion matrix at the balanced-accuracy threshold (a), calibration curve (b) and precision/recall/F1 versus decision threshold (c).
Permutation importance for the selected salary model (LightGBM).
Permutation importance for the selected AI-adoption model (LightGBM).
SHAP summary of the LightGBM salary model: each dot is a respondent; colour = feature value; x = effect on predicted log-compensation.
SHAP summary of the LightGBM AI-adoption model (effect on log-odds of using AI).
Partial dependence: average predicted pay as professional experience is varied, by country (a); average predicted AI-adoption probability as age is varied (b).
Hold-out error of the salary model by country (a), experience band (b) and job role (c); India highlighted in orange.
Hold-out ROC-AUC of the AI-adoption classifier within age brackets (a), countries (b) and roles (c); dashed line = overall AUC.
